title: BUILT CoLAB takes part in buildingSMART Portugal working groups

content:
The BUILT CoLAB team is currently taking part in four working groups promoted by buildingSMART Portugal, contributing to the development of reference frameworks, content and resources aimed at supporting the consistent adoption of the BIM and BIM-LCA methodology in the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operation (AECO) sector.

This participation is part of BUILT CoLAB's strategy to promote the digital and sustainable transformation of the construction sector, through collaboration with national and international entities, knowledge sharing and the development of solutions aligned with openBIM principles, as is the case with buildingSMART Portugal.

BIM Competency Framework Working Group

This initiative aims to develop a national taxonomy for defining professional profiles, knowledge areas and standard teaching modules applicable to the AECO sector. The work seeks to ensure alignment with international and European standardisation, linking it to existing national reference frameworks.

This “framework” aims to contribute to the harmonisation of practices, support the qualification of professionals and facilitate the consistent adoption of the BIM methodology in Portugal. It was created in partnership with the BIM Standardisation Technical Committee — CT 197 – BIM, and is coordinated by Miguel Azenha (UMinho).

EIR III Working Group — Exchange Information Requirements for construction

This group is dedicated to drawing up Exchange Information Requirements (EIR) specific to the construction phase, seeking to create a reference framework that supports the clear definition of the information to be produced, exchanged and delivered throughout this stage of the development life cycle.

The initiative continues the work developed by buildingSMART Portugal in creating guidelines for BIM procurement and implementation across different project and construction phases and contexts, coordinated by Miguel Azenha (UMinho).

Construction Product Data Templates Working Group

This working group aims to develop standardised product data templates (PDTs) for construction products, promoting a common structure for organising and exchanging information.

The availability of structured and consistent information on products is an important contribution to their use in BIM and openBIM processes, facilitating interoperability and data integration throughout the life cycle of developments. It is coordinated by Miguel Azenha (UMinho).

Sustainability Working Group

This working group aims to promote the integration of sustainability, circularity and environmental performance principles into openBIM processes, exploring the link between digital information, sustainability indicators and building performance assessment throughout their life cycle.

This work is highly relevant for the adoption of the new energy performance of buildings directive, which mandates zero-emission buildings (ZEB) from 2028 for public buildings, and 2030 for private buildings. It is coordinated by Vanessa Tavares (BUILT CoLAB) and Ricardo Resende (ISCTE).

BUILT CoLAB's participation in these working groups reinforces the organisation's commitment to developing applied knowledge and reference frameworks relevant to the AECO sector.

Collaboration with buildingSMART Portugal and CT 197 – BIM allows BUILT CoLAB to continue contributing to initiatives geared towards standardisation, the qualification of professionals, the improvement of information exchange processes and the dissemination of good BIM practices. The sustainability group, meanwhile, contributes technical knowledge and experience in the areas of LCA, circularity, BIM-LCA, the European Taxonomy and decarbonisation, promoting the connection between BIM processes and current requirements and methodologies for assessing the environmental performance of buildings.

The work developed in this context is the basis for the adoption of more consistent, interoperable and collaborative digital processes, enabling BUILT CoLAB to continue contributing to the digital and sustainable transformation of the construction sector in Portugal.
